(Codex_R6_F001, 0.95, 5, 0.38, DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.process_round()` only runs failure handling for `responses.items()`. Any active model that does not return a `ModelResponse` is skipped entirely: `detect_failure()` is never called, `get_recovery()` is never called, `role_assignment.record_failure()` is never updated, and the model stays in `_active_models`. A missing PM response therefore does not trigger the PM-abort path and the manager can continue scheduling work to a model that produced nothing., PROPOSED_FIX: Derive the expected responders from the current active/allotted model set, compute `missing_ids = expected_ids - responses.keys()`, and route each missing model through failure handling as `TIMEOUT` or a dedicated `MISSING_RESPONSE` failure before any later bookkeeping., VERIFIED: TRUE)

(Codex_R6_F002, 0.85, 1, 0.57, DESCRIPTION: `process_round()` calls `self.role_assignment.reassign(..., live_fingerprints=self._live_fingerprints)` before `self.update_fingerprints(round_idx, findings, responses)`. That means the next round's role map is computed from stale fingerprints, while `get_allocation()` immediately afterwards uses freshly updated fingerprints from `get_live_models()`. Roles and allocation can therefore be based on different capability snapshots for the same next round., PROPOSED_FIX: Update live fingerprints first, still before appending the current `RoundResult`, and only then call `reassign()` so role assignment and allocation both see the same post-round capability state., VERIFIED: TRUE)

(Codex_R6_F003, 0.78, 1, 0.61, DESCRIPTION: The immune-layer input in `process_round()` collapses failure to `mid not in responses or not responses[mid].parseable`. That ignores failures already detected as `EMPTY`, `TIMEOUT`, `FORMAT`, and `UNDERPERFORM` when the response object exists and is parseable. The health monitor can therefore conclude a model is healthy even while the failure handler is repeatedly penalizing or excluding it., PROPOSED_FIX: Feed the actual detected failure outcome into `record_model_round()` instead of recomputing a weaker proxy. At minimum use `failures.get(mid) is not None`; ideally pass the typed failure category., VERIFIED: TRUE)

(Codex_R6_F004, 0.74, 4, 0.49, DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler.get_recovery()` applies the special PM-abort rule only to `EMPTY`, `TIMEOUT`, and `MALFORMED`. Repeated PM `FORMAT` failures fall through to the ordinary branch (`DEGRADE` / `RETRY_CLARIFIED`) instead of aborting or removing the failed manager. That contradicts the class contract that PM failure is hard-abort behavior for control-path failures, because a PM can keep emitting non-compliant control output and still remain PM., PROPOSED_FIX: Include `FailureType.FORMAT` in the PM-special-case branch, or narrow the documented PM-abort contract so format-noncompliance is explicitly treated as safe., VERIFIED: TRUE)

(Codex_R6_F005, 0.70, 5, 0.64, DESCRIPTION: `approve_deferred_remediation()` applies a queued fix using `round_idx = deferred["round"]`, which is the round where the diagnosis was created, not the round where a human actually approved the fix. It also skips the AUTO path's pre-fix snapshot capture. As a result, damping, verification windows, and regression checks are all anchored to the wrong time, so deferred fixes can be judged as if they were applied several rounds earlier., PROPOSED_FIX: Make approval take the current round index, capture a pre-fix snapshot at approval time, and call `set_remediation_state()` with the real application round rather than the original diagnosis round., VERIFIED: TRUE)

(Codex_R6_F006, 0.64, 6, 0.33, DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler._realloc_depth` is keyed only by `task_id` and is only ever incremented by `record_reallocation()`. There is no reset on round boundaries and no clear-on-success path. If a task ID persists across rounds, the cascade guard becomes a lifetime counter and will eventually block valid reallocations even when each round only needed one retry., PROPOSED_FIX: Scope reallocation depth to `(round_idx, task_id)` or reset the counter when a task finishes or a new round begins., VERIFIED: TRUE)

(Codex_R6_F007, 0.58, 4, 0.68, DESCRIPTION: `apply_diagnosis()` treats a `mu+novelty` disagreement as an "adjustment" and records that stop-signal priority changed to `novelty_rate preferred`, but it does not mutate any config field or decision path. `process_round()` still uses `self.diminishing_returns.stop(round_idx)` exactly as before. The system logs a closed-loop adaptation that has no operational effect., PROPOSED_FIX: Either add a real stop-policy switch that changes how stopping is decided after this diagnosis, or emit this as a pure advisory event instead of recording it as an applied adjustment., VERIFIED: TRUE)

(Codex_R6_F008, 0.55, 5, 0.24, DESCRIPTION: The failure event stream loses important information in `FailureHandler.detect_failure()`: the `FORMAT` branch emits `ManagerEventType.MALFORMED`, and the `UNDERPERFORM` branch emits no event at all. A PM consuming the event stream cannot reliably distinguish parse failures from schema/format failures and may miss sustained underperformance entirely., PROPOSED_FIX: Emit a distinct event for every detected failure type, or at least attach the exact `FailureType` in event metadata for all branches including `UNDERPERFORM`., VERIFIED: TRUE)
